title: Artin-Schreier short exact sequence for arbitrary schemes
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $p$ a prime, and suppose $p\cdot1=0$ in $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. On the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], let $G$ be the universe lift of the associated sheaf of the structure module [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module], an abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. There exist morphisms $\iota:\underline{\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z}\to G$ and $\wp:G\to G$, with zero composite, for which $0\to\underline{\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z}\xrightarrow{\iota}G\xrightarrow{\wp}G\to0$ is short exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. The constant sheaf is that of [def-sc-constant-sheaves]. No field, curve, nonemptiness or affineness assumption is made.

source.place: Opening Artin-Schreier short exact sequence for every scheme in characteristic p, together with the proof of Tag 03PL for local surjectivity.

proof.text: Identify the tensor pullback of the structure module along every etale $u:U\to X$ with the structure module of $U$ using [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf]. Its unit characterization and pullback composition identify the restriction maps with the ring maps on global sections [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial]. Thus $G$ has sections $\operatorname{ULift}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. The equation $p=0$ pulls back along $U\to X$. On nonzero section rings, Frobenius is additive in characteristic $p$; on the zero ring additivity is immediate. Hence $x\mapsto x^p-x$ is a natural additive map $\wp:G\to G$. The prime-field maps define a constant-presheaf map, which extends through sheafification to $\iota$ by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Fermat gives $\iota\wp=0$.

source.place: Opening sequence for a scheme in characteristic p; maps are constructed on sections.

proof.text: *$\wp$ is an epimorphism* (following the proof of the Kummer sequence, Stacks Lemma 03PL). By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] it suffices to show: for every object $U$ of $X_{\Et}$ and $f\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ there is a covering $\{V_i\to U\}$ in $X_{\Et}$ with $f|_{V_i}=y_i^p-y_i$ for some $y_i\in\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal O_{V_i})$. Cover $U$ by affine opens $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ [def-pc-scheme], let $f_i=f|_{U_i}\in A_i$ and $B_i=A_i[T]/(Q_i)$ with $Q_i=T^p-T-f_i$, monic. Its derivative is $Q_i'=pT^{p-1}-1=-1$, a unit, so $A_i[T]_{Q_i'}/(Q_i)=B_i$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-monic-derivative](1). It is of finite type, and every geometric fibre, over $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ with $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field, is $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega[T]/(T^p-T-\bar f_i)$, nonempty because a polynomial of degree $p\geq1$ over a field gives a nonzero quotient ring; so $\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to U_i$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-nonempty-fibres]. Put $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$; the composite $V_i\to U_i\hookrightarrow U\to X$ is etale, since open immersions are etale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] and composites of etale morphisms are etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2), and $V_i\to U$ is a morphism of $X_{\Et}$. The $U_i$ cover $U$ and each $V_i\to U_i$ is surjective, so $\{V_i\to U\}$ is jointly surjective, a covering of $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For $y_i$ the class of $T$ in $B_i$ we have $y_i^p-y_i=f_i=f|_{V_i}$.

source.place: Lemma 03PL (lemma-kummer-sequence), proof: the covering $\underline{\Spec}_U(\mathcal O_U[T]/(T^n-f))\to U$, finite free hence surjective, standard etale; here with $T^p-T-f$, as in the blueprint proof ('For surjectivity: let $U\to C$ be etale ...')

proof.text: *The kernel on stalks.* Let $K\to\mathbf G_a$ be a kernel of $\wp$ in the abelian category $\Ab(X_{\Et})$; as $\wp\circ\iota=0$ (step 1), $\iota$ factors as $\iota=(K\to\mathbf G_a)\circ\iota'$ with $\iota':\mathbf F_p\to K$. Let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. The stalk functor at $\bar x$ is exact [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], so $K_{\bar x}=\ker(\wp_{\bar x})\subseteq(\mathbf G_a)_{\bar x}=\varinjlim_{(U,\bar u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)=:R$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods], where $\wp_{\bar x}[U,\bar u,a]=[U,\bar u,a^p-a]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk], $\mathbf Z/p\to(\mathbf F_p)_{\bar x}$, $c\mapsto[X,\bar x,\eta_X(c)]$, is an isomorphism; composed with $\iota'_{\bar x}$ it is $c\mapsto[X,\bar x,c\cdot1]$. (a) *Injective:* $R\neq0$, since $1=0$ in $R$ would give $1=0$ in some $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ with $U$ nonempty (it receives $\bar u$), impossible; for $c\neq0$ the element $c\cdot1$ is a unit of $R$ ($c$ is invertible in $\mathbf Z/p$), hence nonzero. (b) *Surjective onto $\ker\wp_{\bar x}$:* let $[U,\bar u,a]$ with $[U,\bar u,a^p-a]=0$; after passing to a smaller pointed etale neighbourhood, $a^p=a$ in $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. Let $u\in U$ be the image of $\bar u$. The germ $a_u$ in the local ring $\mathcal O_{U,u}$ satisfies $a_u^p=a_u$ and $p=0$ there, so $a_u=c\cdot1$ for some $c\in\mathbf Z/p$ by [lem-sc-local-ring-artin-schreier-kernel]; hence $a|_W=c\cdot1$ on an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq U$ of $u$. $W\to X$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], and $\bar u$ factors through $W$ (its image point $u$ lies in the open $W$), so $(W,\bar u)$ is a pointed etale neighbourhood over $(U,\bar u)$ and $[U,\bar u,a]=[W,\bar u,c\cdot1]=[X,\bar x,c\cdot1]$. Thus $\iota'_{\bar x}$ is bijective for every geometric point.

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence: 'The kernel of $\wp$ is the constant sheaf $\mathbf F_p$: its stalk at a geometric point $\bar x$ is $\{a: a^p=a\}=\mathbf F_p$'

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By step 3, $\iota':\mathbf F_p\to K$ is an isomorphism on every geometric stalk, hence an isomorphism of $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. So $\iota=(K\to\mathbf G_a)\circ\iota'$ is a kernel of $\wp$; in particular it is a monomorphism and $\operatorname{Im}(\iota)=\operatorname{Ker}(\wp)$. With $\wp\circ\iota=0$ (step 1) and $\wp$ an epimorphism (step 2), the sequence $0\to\mathbf F_p\to\mathbf G_a\to\mathbf G_a\to0$ is short exact by the definition [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Forget the sectionwise descriptions of the two maps; the resulting iota, wp and zero-composite witness satisfy exactly the existential Lean statement.

source.place: ## Proof, last clause: 'therefore $\wp$ is surjective as a morphism of etale sheaves'

lean.statement: theorem exists_artinSchreier_shortExact (X : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : (p : Γ(X, ⊤)) = 0) : let G := (sheafCompose X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}).obj (Modules.etaleTensorSectionsSheaf (Modules.unit X)) ∃ (iota : X.constantZMod p ⟶ G) (wp : G ⟶ G) (hzero : iota ≫ wp = 0), (ShortComplex.mk iota wp hzero).ShortExact
